fields.quoted_span: The petition, if enacted, would end the Statewide prohibition on rent control "by striking out [G. L. c. 40P]" and instituting in its place "a limit on any annual rent increase" set at "the annual increase in Consumer Price Index or [five percent], whichever is lower."
fields.note: The strike of c. 40P, the CPI/5% cap, the art. 48 religion holding, and the remand/injunction are all in the opinion. The June 23, 2026 date appears in the opinion's header. The 'Cella v. Attorney General' name is inferable from the caption (Cella & others vs. Attorney General).

fields.note: The cap of the lower of CPI or 5% matches. 'Never took effect' follows from the petition being barred from the ballot.
The effective_date field is empty. The document states no effective date, and the petition was barred from the ballot, so the empty value is consistent.

fields.quoted_span: art. 48 bars placement of the petition on the November 2026 Statewide election ballot.
fields.note: 'Failed' is consistent with the petition being barred and the court enjoining steps to place it on the ballot.

fields.quoted_span: the petition excludes several categories of residential properties from its definition of "covered dwelling units," including those in "facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes."
fields.note: The opinion supports the statewide scope for covered dwelling units and the educational/religious/nonprofit facility exclusion. The owner-occupied (4 units), 10-year new construction, publicly regulated, and short-term rental exemptions are not in this document (they come only from DX14), so they cannot be verified here. The record flags them as secondary-source only.

fields.quoted_span: challenge the Attorney General's certification of Initiative Petition 25-21, titled "An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases."
fields.note: The petition number and title match. The SJC-13893 docket number appears in the header. The '2026 Massachusetts rent control ballot question' alias is a descriptive label, not a citation in the document.
